survivors.claim: D4 says the deriveState() body is extracted 'by brace matching'; the shipped extractor is `src.indexOf('\n}', at)` — the first newline-brace after the function start, with no depth tracking. It is equivalent to brace matching on all five drivers today, but any future column-0 `}` inside deriveState() (a multi-line template literal, an un-indented nested block) silently truncates the body and hides every banned call after it, with the test still green.
survivors.impact: The structural guard this spec exists to add can be blinded by a formatting change in a driver without anyone noticing.
survivors.evidence: Executed comparison of the heuristic vs a depth-counting brace matcher on live drivers: identical body lengths on all five (3327/618/5569/677/436); D4 text: 'extracts each function body by brace matching'; shipped code: `const end = src.indexOf('\n}', at)`.
